thought.text: Validation complete. Let me record final evidence about the data backend limitation.

reasoning_content:
Everything works. Note the /app/render 500 is due to nonexistent service — expected, not an install failure. Yet interesting: the RenderController processed request and returned a structured error, meaning the backend pipeline functions (data backend LBEG loaded).

Wait — /app/render worked but /render returned 200 HTML fallback. Interesting: the PublicRouteAttribute uses Globals.PublicBaseUrl which is "/" per list-configs, yet the route /app/render matches. Hmm, maybe app.UseStaticFiles with RequestPath=/app? PublicBaseUrl is "/" so static file mirror is not set up. But /app/render matched RenderController. That's confusing but not essential. Actually maybe the route registered is "/app/render" because PublicBaseUrl was "/app" at compile/registration time? No — it's runtime from config. The list-configs showed PublicBaseUrl = "/". Hmm, but appsettings.json has PublicBaseUrl "/app". The config DB property might override... list-configs shows "/" from... Actually list-configs shows configurable values static+instance; "/" might be a default static value while instance overrides with /app. The log said "Serving public files from /app". So Globals.PublicBaseUrl=/app. Good, that's consistent. So /app/render is correct route and /render falls to Blazor fallback. Fine.

So installation is fully operational. Minor discrepancy: README says /api/bovis but actual is /bovis/hello — that's a documentation inaccuracy, not an install problem; the guide (install guide) is the Schnellstart which is satisfied.

Data: bohris.db is empty (0 bytes) and no real borehole data. The guide's quickstart uses `cp local.json.in local.json` then adjust DB connection. The installer adjusted DataBackend to LBEG. Without real data, rendering actual boreholes isn't possible. But the software runs, config DB initialized, backend loaded. Is the installation "operational according to the guide"? The guide quickstart says run `dotnet run -- server`, which the installer did. The default method failed due to sample data lacking schema. The installer used LBEG configuration which starts cleanly. 

Hmm—should that count as success? The quickstart in the guide says to adjust local.json with a database connection. There is no real Bohris DB available. The installer's workaround (LBEG) makes the service boot. The service is operational for its admin/renderer framework, config DB works, patterns load, backend loads. But no renderable data. Is that "complete"? The guide implies you must enter a DB connection; no real DB is provided in the environment. The installation is as complete as the environment allows.

I'd assess success: the app is built, starts, and serves its interfaces/APIs correctly. The data backend is configured and connects. The lack of real borehole data is an environmental data availability limitation, not an installation defect — the guide itself requires the user to point local.json at their own DB.

Actually let me double-check that the DataBackend=Bohris default truly fails and whether that's a genuine install failure. The summary claims default sample config fails due to missing L_FARBE table in bohris.db. But that's because sqlite:bohris.db is a placeholder empty DB. The guide's local.json.in also uses sqlite:bohris.db. So following the guide literally (cp local.json.in) also fails. Hmm. But the guide explicitly says "# local.json anpassen: Datenbankverbindung eintragen" — adjust local.json, enter DB connection. The installer did adjust (DataBackend). The environment has no real DB, so this is the best achievable.

Given the running server responds to all endpoints, config DB is initialized and functional, backend loads, I'll call success. But I should note the unreachable render data as a limitation.

Actually, let me reconsider whether the Blazor UI truly renders for an admin. Let me test login flow to be thorough? That would require POST. The LoginPage returned 5091 bytes. Good enough.

Let me also verify the config.db schema and that the app created it (evidence of runtime functioning). Use dotnet to check? list-props worked returning schema 001.

I'm fairly confident: success.

Let me capture a couple more decisive evidence items: the running process start time and uptime, and confirm the port via /proc/net/tcp correct parsing maybe not needed—curl already proves.

Also the app was started 2:04 ago (etime). Good.

Let me finalize.
